attribution.note: Marcus's own spoken remarks, published on his Substack under his name; not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense claim. The proposition keeps 'all of these companies', the agent-selling scope, 'financial problems' and 'much more' spending than earning. Correctly typed as an observation.

contract.note: The plain reading ('earnings' as revenue, 'much more' as a substantial excess) is ordinary. But Marcus gave no basis, period or full company list. Whether spending means operating costs, net loss or cash including capex decides the result. The Q2 2026 period is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: Anthropic S-1 (Oct 26, 2026). For H1 2026 it shows a GAAP operating loss of about $0.7B on $16.3B revenue and positive adjusted operating income. That is a six-month period, not the target quarter, and it gives no cash or capex figures, so it is context only.

Yahoo report of Q2 2026 GAAP operating income of $974M for Anthropic. This cuts against Marcus on an operating basis, but the same report notes a large H1 net loss on paper and heavy data-centre investment. Without a settled accounting basis it does not decide the claim.

reviews.rationale: The claim covers every agent-selling company, but the packet has no OpenAI figures. Anthropic's Q2 operating profit points against the claim on an operating basis. Its huge H1 net loss and unknown cash and capex spending could point for it. Because the speaker named no accounting basis, and the packet has neither matched data for every company nor a decisive measure, the evidence does not settle the claim.
